name: Living Hell
label: Revelation
lede: Three dead New England hardcore bands became one very dark one: a demo good enough that two labels pressed it, and a Revelation album that ends in five minutes of static.

eras.title: Out of Dead Wrong, Fear Tomorrow and Follow Through
eras.text: Living Hell came together from the wreckage of three New England bands, Dead Wrong, Fear Tomorrow and Follow Through, and aimed squarely at the bleak, metallic Cleveland sound of Integrity. In one year they went from a demo to a Revelation LP.

years.h: Living Hell forms from three New England bands
years.p: Singer Craig Mack, guitarists Seann McKay and Dan Sullivan, bassist Jim Volinski and drummer Jack LaBarca come out of Dead Wrong, Fear Tomorrow and Follow Through.

years.h: Living Hell's demo becomes the Pavor Nocturnis EP
years.p: Living Hell's five-song demo goes over so well that Rock Vegas puts it out on CD and Lockin' Out Records presses it as a red 7", Pavor Nocturnis.
years.xp: A389 Recordings later put the same five songs up digitally, billing the band as Integrity-inspired hardcore.

years.src: Scene Point Blank · Punknews · Revelation Records pressing history · Bandcamp
years.h: The Lost and the Damned · Revelation REV 145
years.p: Twelve songs, from The Resurrection to King of Kings. Scene Point Blank gave it 9 out of 10 and called it one of the year's top hardcore albums.
years.xp:
Reviewers heard Integrity's Dwid in Craig Mack's darker lyrics, and Integrity's Systems Overload in Condemned, Vermin and Fall From Grace. Punknews compared Mack's throaty yell to [[Hatebreed|40b7efb7-1268-4a80-b354-600afdcbe9e2]]'s Jamey Jasta.

Revelation's first vinyl run was 330 on grey and white, 326 on opaque red, and a second press of 110 on black.

years.h: Living Hell end their album on five minutes of static
years.p: King of Kings, the closing track of Living Hell's The Lost and the Damned, trails into more than five minutes of static noise. Punknews' reviewer felt it swamped the music before it.
